text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The government spells out measures that will transform Kenya into an industralised country by the year 2020.
- A Mombasa court is told police have overwhelming evidence a former Kenya Ports Authority managing director and 19 others conspired to defraud the government of revenue.
- Five opposition parliamentarians condemn the massive importation of sugar which has hit Kenya's sugar industry.
- A former police commissioner Bernard Hinga is car-jacked by armed robbers in Nairobi.
- Two passengers and a pedestrian die after a bus loses control in Nairobi.
- A court in Nyeri is told a bandit killed by police ordered his brother to kill a British aid worker.
- Pressure mounts on the chairman of parliament's Public Accounts Committee to resign.
- The government requires all oil companies to import crude oil in joint ventures from June 1.
- The government invites the French to invest in the telecommunications sector once it is liberalised.
- President Daniel arap Moi threatens to jail the minister for Home Affairs and National Heritage William ole Ntimama if he does not stop saying the president fears him.
- Controversy is brewing at the Kenya Farmers Association where farmers do not like the way the current chairman is running the body. ($1=54 Kenyan Shillings)
